parts.title: Part 1 · Dictation
parts.instr: Your teacher reads the dictation. Write what you hear in the box.

parts.title: Part 2 · Listening
parts.instr: Listen to your teacher’s questions. Choose the correct answer (a, b or c).

parts.title: Part 3 · Gap fill
parts.instr: Write ONE word in each gap.

parts.title: Part 5 · Error correction
parts.instr: Correct the mistake in each sentence. You can add one word, take out one word, or change one word. Type the whole corrected sentence.

items.text: In the darkness, we could hear all the mouse moving around, but we couldn’t see them.
I always have to borrow Fiona a pen during the lessons because she never remembers to bring one with her.
I can’t find the gold chain that David gave me nowhere. Have you seen it?
Excuse me, sir. I’m afraid no visiters are allowed in this part of the building. You’re going to have to leave.
This shopping centre is composed with two separate buildings, one on either side of the road, and they’re connected by a bridge.
What would you buy if I would give you £10,000?
My sister and brother aren’t close; they have very little for common.
I’m sorry to make you waiting. I’ll be with you in a minute.
He said his laptop was faulty but, to my opinion, there’s nothing wrong with it.
I think Michela lives with pasta. I never see her eat anything else!

parts.text: The flight only took two hours. The word “mad” means angry, very interested, and crazy. We can use the expression “If I were you” to give advice. Three feet make a yard. The English alphabet is composed of twenty-six letters. The word “towards” means “in the direction of”. The past of “fly” is “flew”. Footballers’ shirts have names and numbers written on their backs. The three forms of “lie” are “lie, lay, lain”. The word “thorough” means “complete”. The verb “give back” means “return”. The words “may” and “might” express the idea of “perhaps”. We can see the film any evening next week.
